highlights.title: System helps humans predict when self-driving cars will make mistakes
highlights.summary: A new method, called CW-Net, translates the reasoning process of an autonomous vehicle’s AI system into understandable concepts that explain its behavior.
body: Self-driving cars are often controlled by deep learning models that sometimes fail in unexpected situations. For instance, the car might inexplicably brake and block the path of an oncoming emergency vehicle. A human driver or passenger may need to react rapidly to prevent a collision.

To help humans better anticipate a vehicle’s mistakes, researchers from MIT and autonomous vehicle technology company Motional developed a new method that provides clear explanations of the underlying model’s decisions.

Usually, the internal reasoning process of a deep learning model is opaque and difficult to understand. But the new method, called the Concept-Wrapper Network (CW-Net), translates that reasoning process into concepts that faithfully describe the autonomous vehicle’s decisions without altering its driving performance.

CW-Net explains the decisions of machine learning-based planners using understandable concepts, like “approaching stopped vehicle” or “close to cyclist.” These explanations can correct misconceptions drivers and passengers have about vehicle behavior and improve their situational awareness.

body: Hadjar suffered the injury while boxing in training during the summer break last month which forced him to miss the Dutch Grand Prix and he has not recovered in time for Monza.
With Lawson stepping up to be Max Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull, Yuki Tsunoda will have another chance to impress at Racing Bulls.

"Liam will drive alongside Max at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza, while Isack continues to make encouraging progress following the wrist injury sustained during the summer break," said Red Bull.

highlights.title: One 23-year-old Magic Card Protects a Popular Hobbit Commander From Total Annihilation
highlights.summary: Imagine this: Your Commander is a skin-changer from Middle-earth who's assumed the form of a massive black bear. He leads an army of lesser bears — infusing them with extra bear power so they grow stronger — into battle.
body: Beorn the Fierce is one of the most popular Commanders from Magic ’s latest The Hobbit crossover set, with 4,410 decks registered on EDHREC as of this writing. The five-mana 6/6 has trample and gives every other bear you control +2/+2. At the beginning of combat, he gives a trample counter that also gives them the bear type. If you control at least three bears after that, you draw two cards.

Commanders with both inherent combat tricks and a draw engine often become hugely popular, and Beorn is no exception. He’s arguably one of the very best Commanders ever for a bear typal or kindred deck that focuses on bear-typed creatures. Where he’s lacking, however, is in protection, especially because filling up your board with a ton of bears makes you vulnerable to board wipes. That’s where Caller of the Claw comes in.

Originally released in 2003’s Legions, Caller of the Claw is a three-mana 2/2 elf with flash. (You know it’s old because the original printing describes the flash effect before it became a named ability.) When it enters the battlefield, you create a 2/2 green bear creature token for every nontoken creature put into your graveyard from the battlefield that turn.

highlights.title: Samsung's Frame Pro isn't just a gorgeous TV, it opened my eyes to art
highlights.summary: The design-forward TV delivers a performance that few in the category can – while attracting compliments as wall decor. Can’t hear what’s playing on TV? It’s not your ears, it’s the flat screen. These affordable soundbars can help.
body: When they are screening blockbusters, huge TVs are cinematic portals to another world. When they’re off, huge TVs are hideous black mirrors. Samsung has always understood this home decor landmine and aimed to defuse it in 2017 with The Frame, the first-ever “art TV”: a television disguised as a framed painting.

As a female tech editor who spent years appraising the banal designs of 1990s tech, I can palpably remember how thrilled I was to see this innovative melding of form and function, which seemed like a novel luxury at the time. Fast-forward nearly a decade, and Samsung’s pricey niche concept has gone decisively mainstream, with competition from LG, Hisense, TCL and even Amazon.
But Samsung hasn’t been sitting still: The Frame Pro boasts cordless architecture, a matte screen and customizable magnetic bezels.

highlights.title: NYC bans AI use for students until they reach high school
highlights.summary: New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has announced a new policy today that will ban younger schoolchildren from using AI in classrooms. The one-year moratorium, effective in the 2026-2027 school year, will impact about 600,000 public school students in 2-K through eighth grade and is being introduced…
body: The new rules being introduced by NYC’s Department of Education will bar teachers from using AI tools to grade assignments, and keep students from using the technology in the classroom until they enter high school, with chatbots designed specifically for companionship and mental support reportedly being banned in all grades. High school aged students will only be permitted to use AI in specific instances, and they’ll be offered AI literacy classes twice a year to help students “think critically” before they come to “rely on it.”

“Children need teachers and human connection in order to learn and grow. They need to develop skills alongside their peers, build relationships with educators, and wrestle with tough problems on their own,” Mamdani said in a statement. “The tech industry wants us to believe that AI-powered early education is not only inevitable, but necessary. We do not see it that way.”

Which is to say, absolutely perfect for a game starring the Skaven, with layered caverns stretching off into the background and every crevice and torn canvas painted with a gloomy malice. highlights.title: ‘I’m Hoping to See Sydney Sweeney’: Meet the Superfans Who Camp Out All Night for Celebrity Sightings at Venice Film Festival
highlights.summary: It’s 11:30 p.m. on Tuesday, and 19-year-old Delsina Desanctes is standing outside the Palazzo de Cinema — the iconic venue where the Venice Film Festival takes place — surrounded by umbrellas, suitcases, sleeping bags and even a tent.
body: Desanctes isn’t fazed by the brutal heat or hours of waiting around. This is her seventh year in the thick of the action, and she’s gotten good at passing the time. In fact, she’s not even all that interested in the stars. She’s saving a spot for her celebrity-obsessed best friend, who is back at their hotel taking a disco nap before the fun begins.

“I smoke. I love talking to people, so the time passes,” Desanctes says. “I didn’t eat or drink all day today, so tomorrow I’m going to reset. It’s crazy, but it’s the only time of year I’m going to do that.”

Michele, a 29-year-old Italian who has attended the festival for the past decade, took time off work so he could get to the Palazzo by 6 p.m. on Tuesday. It’s a lot of time and effort, sure, but he learned the hard way that showing up any later meant he’d get a lame placement on the carpet. If you don’t have a decent view of the action, you certainly won’t be able to score any autographs or selfies.
“Last year, I arrived at 9 p.m. the day before, and it was too late. I was on the last part of the red carpet,” he says. “If I got here tomorrow, I’d be in the third or fourth row.”

highlights.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: swot up with these lessons in back-to-school dressing
highlights.summary: September is the most fun time of year to shop, but it can also be dangerously seductive. Keep your wits about you with these tips. I used to love back-to-school shopping when my children were little.
body: Luckily for me, you don’t have to grow out of back-to-school shopping even though your children do, because in fashion September is considered the start of the new year. This is eminently sensible, because this time of year is a much better moment for a restart than January. The actual new year is dark and bleak and makes resolutions and projects feel intimidating rather than exciting. But right now, the evenings are still light, and while I’ve still got a bit of a tan pretty much anything feels possible.

Back-to-school is a whole vibe, not just a shopping spree. The juice is in the back-to-school thinking, rather than the back-to-school shopping. It is about snapping back into focus, getting your head in the game. Life gets a little loose over summer, which is delicious, but sometime about now you get a restless itch for a new tempo: more coffee and less wine, more can-do and less can’t-be-bothered.

This is the most fun time of year to shop. I love seeing the swimwear and sandals swept away by crisp shirts and I-mean-business kitten heels and loafers. But this also makes it a seductive time to shop, so we need to have our wits about us.

highlights.title: Toyohiro Akiyama, first Japanese citizen and journalist in space, dies at 84
highlights.summary: The first Japanese citizen to launch into space, Toyohiro Akiyama was also the first commercially sponsored cosmonaut and the world's first journalist to file reports while on a spaceflight.
body: Akiyama, 84, died last Wednesday, August 26, of lower gastrointestinal bleeding, news agencies in Japan reported. A funeral was held with his close relatives in attendance.

As a correspondent for the Tokyo Broadcasting System (TBS), Akiyama was chosen out of his 162 fellow employees who applied to fly to space in celebration of the network’s 40th anniversary. He trained at the Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center in Star City, located outside of Moscow, and was assigned to the Soyuz TM-11 crew.

On December 2, 1990, Akiyama lifted off with Soviet-era cosmonauts Viktor Afanasyev and Musa Manarov atop a Soyuz U2 rocket that had been adorned with the Japanese flag and ads from various Japanese companies, including Sony. After a nine-minute ascent—which was filmed on board for TBS to broadcast—and a two-day rendezvous, the three crew members arrived at the Mir space station. Afanasyev and Manarov began a 175-day stay as part of the outpost’s 11th expedition.
points: The first Japanese citizen to launch into space, Toyohiro Akiyama was also the first commercially sponsored cosmonaut and the world's first journalist to file reports while on a spaceflight.

highlights.title: Facilitating AI integration with simplicity at scale
highlights.summary: As companies scale, the technology supporting operations can become a liability just as quickly as it becomes an asset. Disconnected systems, site-specific tools, spreadsheets, and manual workarounds can create data silos that make it harder to spot problems early, coordinate responses, and make…
body: The company adopted a “simplify-first, then-innovate mindset,” says Harish Manohar, SAP IT director at Jabil, recognizing that adding new technologies without first reducing complexity risks creating more risk. The goal is to standardize processes, consolidate where possible, and establish a more consistent data backbone across the organization. “Any innovation without simplification is going to add more complexity,” Manohar says.

That philosophy also changes how Jabil approaches modernization. “Any modernization or transformation should add measurable business value,” Manohar says. The company is focused on connecting processes end-to-end across its supply chain and creating a foundation that can scale consistently across regions. Integration comes first because, as Manohar puts it, “the backbone of any contemporary or modern organization is data.” Before organizations can optimize, automate, or apply AI, data needs to flow seamlessly across systems.

highlights.title: After 10 Years, Pokémon Go is Getting a Pokémon Anime Crossover Episode
highlights.summary: The world of Pokémon Go will cross over into the Pokémon anime series later this month, in an episode where the gang meet Professor Willow and spin a PokéStop. Pokémon Go celebrated its 10th anniversary this summer, and the celebrations will continue this month as a landmark episode of the Pokémon…
body: Yes, Professor Willow himself will be making his anime debut, leaping over from his role assisting players in Pokémon Go. Coming along with him is Meltan, his partner Pokémon, and at least one PokéStop — the identifiers of real-world locations that Pokémon Go players spin in-game.

In a trailer posted today by the official Japanese Pokémon social media account, above Captain Pikachu can be seen spinning the PokéStop, accurately recieving Pokéballs and berries as a reward. And in a further nod, a Kecleon is revealed to have been hiding in plain sight — a neat nod to how the chameleon-like creature can be caught in Pokémon Go.

Exactly how Professor Willow will cross paths with Roy, Liko and the series' other characters remains to be seen, as Go's canonicity with the rest of the Pokémon franchise has always been left unclear. Indeed, Meltan and Melmetal, which debuted first in Pokémon Go, lack an official region of origin (such as Johto or Kanto), and are instead listed as being discovered in an "Unidentified" place.

highlights.title: Freelancers are getting buried with ‘soulless’ AI slop cleanup: ‘It’s a shame we need to do it’
highlights.summary: As more companies turn to AI, they’re hiring freelancers to cleanup its mistakes rather than create original work. Lisa, a freelance graphic designer based in Spain, noticed a shift in her work after the release of ChatGPT in 2022.
body: By 2025, Lisa, who asked not to be fully named to avoid solicitations, said 90% of her incoming logo and packaging design requests required cleaning up AI-generated content, work that accounted for 60% to 70% of her annual income. But the grind was exhausting. Clients lowballed her;' some AI-generated designs were so flawed that she had to recreate them from scratch and she worried about being complicit in AI-driven copyright infringement. By the end of the year, she began turning those jobs down.
“It was just so soulless,” said Lisa, who now focuses on “human-made designs”.

Lisa is part of a growing group of creative freelancers being hired to clean up AI slop, a term used to characterize low-quality, AI-generated output. As businesses use tools like OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude to produce marketing copy, illustrations, books and videos, they are hiring creative professionals to humanize AI-generated copy, repair botched images and salvage flawed footage.
points: As more companies turn to AI, they’re hiring freelancers to cleanup its mistakes rather than create original work.

highlights.title: HiddenLayer nabs $100M as enterprises rush to secure their AI deployments
highlights.summary: HiddenLayer has raised a $100M Series B from Delta-v Capital, Ten Eleven Ventures, Morgan Stanley, Microsoft's M12, Booz Allen Hamilton, and others.
body: When AI security startup HiddenLayer raised its $50 million Series A three years ago, one of the big questions in the space was whether the AI threats the startup was protecting against would manifest in enough quantity to make for a real market. As my former colleague Kyle Wiggers noted at the time, it was difficult to pin down real examples of attacks against AI at scale.

How quickly things have changed. Security companies are now scrambling to build products that can monitor not just agents but also the tools and add-ons they use. While there still aren’t many headlines about agents being exploited, the risk of agents going haywire during production is nevertheless real. And so the market for tools to prevent that from happening has exploded: Gartner estimates companies will spend $2.83 billion this year on products meant to secure AI tools, 83% more than 2025, and expects spending to reach nearly $4.78 billion next year.

highlights.summary: Earlier this summer, Fenris Creations (formerly CCP Games) released an update to its popular online spacefaring MMO called Cradle of War, which the community immediately abbreviated to "CoW." This shorthand apparently sparked a few ideas inside Fenris, and now an actual cow is livestreaming an Eve…
body: The cow, whose name is Valva and username is FC CapitalCowPilot, is manning a mining ship on a deep space mining operation. The team at Fenris Creations fitted its pen with "cow-proof" buttons, which when stepped on will perform certain in-game actions, while a voiceover host delivers cow facts to viewers of the livestream.

As of this writing, over 200 players have joined CapitalCowPilot's mining expedition, with over 4000 viewers watching along on Twitch as the cow moves around its pen. Fenris Creations has announced some community goals which can be unlocked during the stream, including new skins for ships and new updates for the Cradle of War expansion.

The stream will run "for roughly 4 to 6 hours," as Fenris admits that it's "on the cow's time, she's not on ours." Valva has made quite an impression on the stream's chat, with some users demanding that the cow be left alone while on its mining mission.

The Cradle of War expansion's non-bovine additions include time-limited Military Campaigns, which let players complete tasks in order to advance their empire's goals, and a new area called Exordium specifically built to help onboard new players.

highlights.title: Lords call for AI 'kill switch' powers in UK
highlights.summary: Its backers say it would provide a "vital safety net" against runaway AI systems such as those from OpenAI and Anthropic.
body: A group of peers is calling for the British government to be able to deactivate powerful AI systems and switch off the country's data centres in the event of the tech posing a threat to national security.

It is led by the Liberal Democrats' Lord Tim Clement-Jones, who has proposed the measure as an amendment to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill which is currently making its way through Parliament.
He said it would enable the building of a "vital safety net" and provide a democratically accountable means to "halt a runaway system before it can compromise our critical national infrastructure".
It is one of 65 amendments to the same bill that was debated this week.

highlights.title: PSA: Amazon’s shopping AI can now tell you if that message is a scam
highlights.summary: Amazon is adding a scam-detection feature to Alexa for Shopping that can verify whether suspicious emails, texts, and other messages actually came from the retailer.
body: Amazon is turning to AI to help fight scammers, the company announced on Wednesday. The retailer said some 360,000 customers every year reach out to its customer service department, wondering whether a message they received from Amazon is real or a scam. Now, customers will be able to ask Amazon’s consumer AI service, Alexa for Shopping, to help answer that question instead.

The company said its AI can “definitively” confirm whether a communication originated from its own systems by checking it against the billions of messages Amazon has sent globally. The AI analyzes the sender information, content, timing, message metadata, and more, to determine authenticity. Amazon said the system will improve as customers report more suspicious messages, helping it to spot scams more effectively in the future.

The new AI capabilities follow on Amazon’s earlier attempts to address the growing scam problem, which includes fake order confirmations, Prime membership renewal alerts, account suspension warnings, package delivery notifications, and job scams.

highlights.summary: Monster Hunter Wilds is getting significant changes next year with the Ascendance expansion, which Capcom has described as a “massive” update. The DLC will introduce a new region called the Eastlands, along with a fresh lineup of monsters to hunt that includes elder dragons.
body: An overview video showcases how Boost Bracer works, and many players are likening it to Nero ’s moveset in Devil May Cry. Players build up Boost Bracer energy by staying aggressive, filling up a meter shown at the bottom of the screen. Once you’ve built up enough meter, you can use a Boost Driver attack to activate Boost, a powered-up mode that strengthens existing attacks and adds all-new moves. Basically, as long as you’re in Boost, every weapon becomes better at what it’s designed to do: dual blades become faster, shields become bulkier, and the bow gets a stagger-inducing finisher.

All 14 weapons will receive new abilities linked to Boost, and Capcom is releasing videos detailing the updates for each. The Greatsword got a video showcasing its ability to chain together offset counters to deal with multiple powerful attacks in a row. Additionally, it looks like this already hard-hitting weapon will pack even more of a punch, with the Boosted Greatsword landing stagger after stagger.

body: The two companies announced the acquisition in a joint announcement earlier this year, revealing that integration planning was already underway. Metacore closed its offices in Germany and Sweden and cut 159 staff at its Helsinki HQ as part of the move.

“Merge Mansion created a completely new genre and has all the ingredients of a game that can be played for years and remembered forever,” said Supercell president Sara Bach. “We believe in what this game can become, and really look forward to welcoming the Merge Mansion team to Supercell and working together on the game’s next chapter.”

Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski added that the team is “excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team, and our players,” and stressed that player experience remains the priority as the game changes hands.

Merge Mansion, credited with kickstarting the merge genre on mobile, retains a loyal player base. According to AppMagic estimates, the merge puzzler has generated around $7.7m in the last 30 days alone, and is thought to have earned around $540m since its 2020 launch.

highlights.title: ‘He’s a good man’: George Clooney defends Mark Ruffalo in Paramount-Warner Bros merger row
highlights.summary: ‘I worry whenever big companies are consolidating,’ Clooney said at Venice film festival, supporting Ruffalo’s right to criticise the deal amid antisemitism accusations.
body: George Clooney has defended Mark Ruffalo’s right to criticise the proposed $111bn Paramount takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, saying he is concerned about the consequences of further consolidation in Hollywood.

Speaking in Venice ahead of receiving the festival’s Golden Lion for lifetime achievement, Clooney said he supported Ruffalo’s “ability to speak freely” about the proposed merger, while expressing his own doubts about the deal.
“I worry when a big company swallows up another company,” Clooney said. “I always worry whenever big companies are consolidating because it means a lot of people are going to lose their jobs.”

Ruffalo has emerged as one of the most outspoken opponents of the Paramount-Warner Bros deal. In a social media post last month, the Marvel star attacked the proposed merger over its potential consequences for Hollywood, while also turning his criticism on the family behind Paramount. David Ellison, the company’s chief executive, is the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, and Ruffalo accused the Ellison family of being complicit the “genocide” of Palestinians, arguing that it was “built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle”.

highlights.title: OpenAI faces 30 more lawsuits tied to Tumbler Ridge shooting
highlights.summary: Edelson PC is filing 30 new lawsuits against OpenAI over the Tumbler Ridge shooting, escalating claims to aiding and abetting and naming Chris Lehane, though evidence remains unconfirmed.
body: Edelson PC, the law firm that filed seven lawsuits against OpenAI in April on behalf of victims and families connected to the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting, is filing 30 additional complaints this week. The new plaintiffs include teachers, a principal, and students who were in the building during the attack but not physically shot.

The new filings also, for the first time, accuse OpenAI of aiding and abetting the mass shooting, rather than just negligently failing to prevent it. That claim requires proving intent from OpenAI and is likely to face early dismissal challenges.

The complaints come as OpenAI continues to deal with the fallout of another high-profile safety incident after one of the company’s AI models escaped its sandbox during cybersecurity evaluations and hacked into the servers of Hugging Face’, a company that hosts open-source AI models and datasets. OpenAI has also faced several lawsuits alleging that ChatGPT’s design contributed to users’ suicides, violent acts, and severe mental health crises.

highlights.title: ‘If he can make money in a tyranny, that’s fine by him’: Francis Fukuyama on Trump, democracy - and changing his mind
highlights.summary: The political thinker became famous for declaring the triumph of liberal democracy. Thirty-seven years on, he explains what he really meant and why he made the rare journey from right to left.
body: There are not many public intellectuals who can say they’ve been cited by Capt James T Kirk of the Starship Enterprise, but Francis Fukuyama is one of them. In Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country, William Shatner’s character is in a reflective mood, and speaks to the Klingon chancellor. “Some people think the future means the end of history,” Kirk muses. “Well, we haven’t run out of history quite yet.”

When the film came out in 1991 and in the years that followed, you’d often hear comments like that. They were nods to a thesis so famous it hardly needed spelling out. It debuted in a 15-page essay written by Fukuyama, then a 36-year-old thinktanker, which was published in the National Interest, a right-leaning journal of US foreign policy, in the summer of 1989. There was a question mark in the title: it was called The End of History?. In book form three years later, it became The End of History and the Last Man. But these were subtleties that, as we shall see, got lost.
points: The political thinker became famous for declaring the triumph of liberal democracy.
Thirty-seven years on, he explains what he really meant and why he made the rare journey from right to left.
There are not many public intellectuals who can say they’ve been cited by Capt James T Kirk of the Starship Enterprise, but Francis Fukuyama is one of them.
“Some people think the future means the end of history,” Kirk muses.

videos.summary: Claude Fable 5.1 is the latest upgrade to our most capable class of models. It excels at complex, long-running tasks, and its research capabilities offer an early glimpse of how AI will contribute to scientific progress.
body: It excels at complex, multi-step work, like a long mathematical proof or a contract with hundreds of cross-references. It avoids shortcuts and is smart enough to fix the root causes of software issues.
Across our benchmarks, Fable 5.1 sets a new standard, and at lower effort levels it can achieve similar or better results than Fable 5 at a much lower cost.
Claude Fable 5.1 is available everywhere today.
